message.content:
Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (one prior commit 9f46912 for Step 1; Step 2's changes are uncommitted — do not commit, do not stage, do not modify anything, though you may read/investigate freely). Build mode. This is SFCC-91 Step 2 of 4: a new atom, `ZimmColourSwatch`, at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (4 new files) plus a 2-line registration edit to `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

You may re-verify anything below yourself via Read/Grep/Glob/Bash.

## Orchestrator's verdict (already run)

**IN SCOPE.** Exactly the 4 planned new files plus a confirmed 2-line (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions, 0 deletions) edit to the theme registration. Both hard-stop paths (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — Step 1's already-committed file; `overrides/app/theme/foundation/**` — Tier 1) confirmed completely untouched. `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` confirmed not created. No data-fetching hook anywhere in the new component (pure presentational leaf, consistent with this codebase's container/presentational rule). Recipe export name confirmed to be exactly `ZimmColourSwatch`, not relying on `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `INTENTIONAL_MERGES` allow-list (still just `['Button','Header','ListMenu']`).

## Tester's findings (already run — extremely thorough, used real Playwright/Chromium and real axe-core runs, not just jsdom)

**🔴 CONFIRMED must-fix — Finding A:** `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31` sets `backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-background-02)'`. This CSS custom property **does not exist anywhere in the codebase**. The actually-registered token (confirmed directly in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:53-59`) is `--zimm-color-bg-01` through `--zimm-color-bg-07` — never `--zimm-color-background-NN`. A repo-wide grep for `zimm-color-background` returns exactly two hits, both inside this step's own two files (the recipe itself, and its own test asserting the same wrong string back at itself) — nothing else in the codebase has ever used this name. I (the orchestrating session, not the Tester) independently re-ran this exact check myself just now and confirm the same result directly from `zimmTokens.ts`.

The Tester proved the real-world consequence in an actual Chromium browser via Playwright (not jsdom): a swatch styled with the real token `var(--zimm-color-bg-02)` renders `rgb(246, 244, 241)` (correct — ivory[200], #f6f4f1). The SAME swatch styled with the recipe's actual (wrong) value `var(--zimm-color-background-02)` renders `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` — fully transparent. This is correct per the CSS spec: `var()` referencing an undefined custom property with no fallback invalidates the whole declaration, and `background-color`'s initial value is transparent. **The swatch's background never renders ivory in any real browser — it is always transparent**, for all three states (Unselected/Selected/Focus), since the declaration is unconditional in `baseStyle`.

Critically, this defect passed every other automated gate clean: `tsc` (it's a syntactically valid string), `eslint` (no such rule exists), `audit:tokens` (Tester proved via a stash-differential re-run that the script only flags raw hex/px/rem/em literals, and has zero concept of validating a `var(--zimm-*)` name against the real token registry — so a plausible-looking but nonexistent name is invisible to it), `recipeGuards.test.ts` (only checks for *bare* Chakra token keys like `'text.default'`, never `var()` string validity), `recipeParts.test.ts` (unrelated — only checks structural part-key coverage, which this recipe does correctly), and even the component's OWN regression-guard test in `index.test.tsx:112` — which only asserts the resolved value equals the literal string `'var(--zimm-color-background-02)'`, and jsdom echoes back whatever text is in a declaration whether or not the named variable is real, so that test passes while asserting on a broken value.

Tester's own visual-checkpoint prediction, worth weighing carefully: in Storybook, all three stories use a real placeholder photo that fully covers the swatch box once loaded (`background-size: cover`), so **this defect will almost certainly be invisible in a normal visual review** — it would only surface via network throttling (catching the pre-paint transparent flash) or a failed image load (which would then show as fully see-through rather than an ivory fallback).

**🟡 should-fix, pre-existing, NOT this step's file to fix — Finding B:** `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`/`PROP_COMBINATIONS` fuzzing harness (lines ~217-243) hardcodes exactly `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}` as its boolean-varying keys — `selected` is not among them. Tester independently reproduced this by writing a throwaway probe that called this recipe's actual `baseStyle` with all 32 of the guard's real generated combinations and confirmed `selected` is never present/true in any of them — meaning the automated guard never walks this recipe's `selected: true` (bottom-border) branch at all. Separately, manual read confirms that branch IS token-clean on its own merits (`var(--zimm-border-width-default)`, `var(--zimm-color-border-focus)` — both confirmed to exist and resolve correctly). Two distinct findings, not one: even if the guard did walk `selected: true`, it still wouldn't have caught Finding A, because it checks for *bare Chakra keys*, never `var()` name validity — a completely different failure class. This is a Tier 2 test-infrastructure gap outside this step's file manifest.

**🔵 note, not a defect:** the regression-guard test's own inline comment predicts a mutation would produce the literal text "bay blue" as the failure value; Tester actually ran the mutation (real before/after, reverted cleanly) and the real failure value was `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` instead, because "bay blue" (two words, spaces) is an invalid CSS colour keyword and the whole declaration gets dropped rather than the literal string being echoed. The guard still correctly fails when it should — this is a comment-accuracy nit, not a functional problem.

**Other things Tester confirmed clean, independently, not just accepted:** href-present vs href-absent branches carry an identical a11y surface (role/aria-checked/aria-label/tabIndex, checked line-by-line); zero real a11y violations via a live axe-core run against the actual rendered component; `ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink)` is module-scoped, not recreated per render; the Storybook story correctly adds a local `MemoryRouter` decorator; no data-fetching hook anywhere; no premature Step 3/4 coupling; `parts: ['swatch','image']` correctly covers every `styles.*` read (confirmed both by direct read and by `recipeParts.test.ts`'s own passing case for this recipe); `theme/components/index.ts` edit independently re-confirmed as exactly 2 insertions.

**What Tester could not verify:** the full `build-storybook` + `test-storybook --ci` pipeline end-to-end (substituted a direct real axe-core run instead — same engine/ruleset, not byte-identical to the full CI path); the `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*.yml` rules directly (a CLI config-resolution error unrelated to this step's content — the underlying accessibility question was already answered by direct reading instead); whether the code comment's claim that "the caller filters out unpopulated-image variations before rendering this component" holds, since no caller exists yet (Step 3/4 territory, can't verify a claim about unwritten code).

## Provenance note, for your own weighing

The wrong token name (`var(--zimm-color-background-02)`) was specified verbatim in the orchestrating session's own launch instructions to the Implementer for this step — the Implementer built exactly what it was told to build. The orchestrating session had verified the *border*-tier token naming convention directly from `zimmTokens.ts` before writing that instruction, but extrapolated the *background*-tier name by analogy rather than checking it directly, and that assumption was wrong. This is disclosed so you don't misattribute the defect's origin — it doesn't change whether the defect is real (it is, triple-confirmed) or whether it needs fixing before this step can PASS.

## Your job

Score against your six axes and return PASS or REWORK. Given a triple-independently-confirmed (registry read + repo-wide grep + real-browser computed-style proof) rendering defect that makes the swatch's background always transparent instead of the intended ivory fill, in a value that is unconditional across all three states this recipe exists to distinguish — walk through what your Correctness and Design fidelity axes should conclude, explicitly, rather than defaulting to a generic verdict. If REWORK, give the specific, minimal instruction the next Implementer round needs (which exact string, in which exact file(s), needs to change to which exact value, and whether the test file's matching literal-string assertion needs the identical correction) — the fix should be a token-name substitution only, not a broader rework of the recipe's structure, since everything else about the recipe (the bottom-border logic, the focus-ring mirroring, the deliberate backgroundColor-from-name omission, the two-part structure) tested clean.

Also state plainly whether Finding B (the recipeGuards fuzzing gap) and the 🔵 comment nit should be carried forward as informational items rather than blocking this step's eventual PASS once Finding A is fixed.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for a single PDP colour swatch — a clickable rectangle filled with that colour
5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,
6	 * background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic
7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on
8	 * why that one `__css` spread stays dynamic.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for the three states this recipe distinguishes, not
11	 * estimated from surrounding metadata — Unselected (node 40000307:13826), Selected
12	 * (40000307:13831), Focus (40002689:3839), all under `size=Large/Rectangle`.
13	 */
14	export const ZimmColourSwatch = {
15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-background-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent
45	      // anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring, and the asymmetry reads as that one
46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors
47	      // zimmNavItem.css.ts's own focus-ring block instead: a uniform `outline` + `outlineOffset`
48	      // pair, applied independently of `selected` above — a swatch can be focused without being
49	      // selected, and selected without being focused. `--zimm-focus-ring` already composites the
50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.
52	      _focusVisible: {
53	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
54	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
55	      },
56	    },
57	    image: {
58	      display: 'block',
59	      width: '100%',
60	      height: '100%',
61	      backgroundSize: 'cover',
62	      backgroundPosition: 'center',
63	      backgroundRepeat: 'no-repeat',
64	    },
65	  }),
66	};
67

1	/**
2	 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
3	 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
4	 *
5	 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
6	 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
7	 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
8	 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
9	 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base

/**
 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
 *
 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
 *
 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
 *
 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
 * walks the component source.
 *
 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
 *
 * It is not a whole-repo guard, and nothing else covers the remainder: the model is strictly
 * sibling-based (a recipe's `parts` are reconciled against the `index.tsx` beside it), so a
 * recipe that does not sit next to its component is out of reach. `theme/components/header.ts`
 * is the only multipart recipe in that position today and is therefore unguarded.
 * `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` does not pick it up either — that suite has no
 * parts-vs-reads check of any kind; it guards bare token keys and recipe namespacing.
 *
 * `READ_RE` recognises only the identifier `styles`, so a second binding in the same component
 * is invisible here: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` reads `chrome.actions`. That one is
 * deliberately out of scope rather than a gap to close — `chrome` holds *ZimmModal's* recipe,
 * so the sibling model would misattribute `actions` to `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts`, which
 * correctly does not declare it.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const COMPONENTS = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'overrides/app/components');

const walk = (dir: string): string[] =>
  readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);
    return entry.isDirectory() ? walk(full) : [full];
  });

/** `parts: ['root', 'label']` — the literal array in a `.css.ts` recipe. */
const PARTS_RE = /\bparts:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]/;
/** `styles.label` and `styles['label']`, the two ways a component reads a resolved part. */
const READ_RE = /\bstyles(?:\.([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)|\[\s*'([^']+)'\s*\])/g;

content.text:
I independently reproduced every load-bearing claim before scoring: read all four new files directly, grepped `zimmTokens.ts` and the whole repo for the token name in question, cross-checked every *other* `var(--zimm-*)` reference in the same recipe against the registry, ran `tsc --noEmit` and the actual `vitest` suite myself, read `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s fuzzing-harness source to verify Finding B's mechanism from first principles, and confirmed the diff-stat and hard-stop-path claims via `git diff`/`git status` myself rather than trusting the summary.

## Per-axis verdict

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **FAIL** | The recipe's own docstring states its purpose: encode Figma values "for the three states this recipe distinguishes" (Unselected/Selected/Focus). `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31` sets the one property common to all three (`backgroundColor`) to `var(--zimm-color-background-02)` — a string that resolves to nothing in any browser, ever, because no CSS custom property of that name is ever defined (confirmed: `zimmTokens.ts` registers `--zimm-color-bg-01` through `-07`, never `-background-`; repo-wide grep finds the string nowhere outside this step's own two files). Per CSS spec, `var()` referencing an undefined custom property with no fallback invalidates the whole declaration; for a non-inherited property like `background-color` this computes to its initial value, `transparent`. The swatch's fill is therefore **always transparent, in every one of the three states this component exists to render** — this is not a partial or edge-case mismatch, it is total, unconditional non-fidelity on the recipe's primary declared purpose. |
| **Correctness** | **FAIL** | Your bar is explicit: "no 🔴 findings from the Tester." There is one, and I reproduced its root cause myself rather than taking it on faith. I ran `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean, zero errors) and the full relevant `vitest` scope myself — `index.test.tsx`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`, `theme/index.test.tsx` — and got 152/152 green, *reproducing* the false-positive, not just hearing about it. The stderr noise I personally observed (`Could not parse CSS stylesheet`, emitted exactly on the swatch's own test and on `theme/index.test.tsx`) corroborates why: jsdom never resolves `var()`, it echoes the literal declaration text back verbatim, so a test asserting `toBe('var(--zimm-color-background-02)')` (`index.test.tsx:112`) passes regardless of whether that name is real. Green `tsc`, green `npm run test`, and a green regression-guard test are not evidence of correctness here — the regression guard is asserting on the same defect it was written to catch. |
| **Pass criteria** | **FAIL** | Same root cause, third angle: a criterion (implicit, but load-bearing — "renders per Figma's Unselected/Selected/Focus states," which is the entire reason this recipe file exists) is asserted-as-met by the test suite but not actually met. Per your own rubric: "Every criterion in the step is met, **with evidence — not asserted**." The evidence I gathered independently (registry read + repo grep + reproduced vacuous test pass) shows the assertion is false. |
| **Completeness** | PASS, one dependency | Story present and correctly scoped (`index.stories.tsx`, `Commerce/ZimmColourSwatch` — correct category per `components.md`'s table, consistent with `SwatchGroup` already living there). Test present and correctly scoped per `testing.md` (href presence/absence, `aria-checked`, `tabIndex`, image-URL mapping, plus the deliberate regression guard). Nothing is *missing* — the defect is a wrong value shared by two files, not an absent deliverable, so I'm not double-failing this axis for the same root cause. But the fix is not the recipe file alone: `index.test.tsx:112`'s assertion must be corrected in the same round or the suite reports green while still validating nothing real. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | Verified directly, not inferred: correct tier chosen (a real `var(--zimm-*)` form, not a bare key or hardcoded hex — the *mechanism* is right, only the *value* is wrong); correct co-location pattern (`<name>.css.ts` beside the component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`); namespacing guard passed under my own test run (`ZimmColourSwatch` doesn't silently inherit any base SFCC recipe); `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` is a generic sibling-based walk (not hardcoded per-recipe — I located and read it, it's actually at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`, not under `theme/components/` as the Tester's report path implied) and mechanically covers this component's `parts: ['swatch','image']` against its actual `styles.*` reads without needing a named test case; import of `RouteLink` matches the established `swatch-group/swatch.jsx` precedent; folder structure matches the decided `ui-kits/atoms/<camelCase>/` convention. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator's verdict is IN SCOPE (not OVER/UNDER), which per your rubric is what this axis takes its evidence from. I independently re-confirmed the diff-stat (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions, 0 deletions in `theme/components/index.ts`), confirmed `git status`/`git diff` show zero touch on `product-view/index.tsx` or `theme/foundation/**`, confirmed `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` does not exist, and grepped for any external consumer of `ZimmColourSwatch`/`zimmColourSwatch` — found none outside its own folder and the one registration import, so there's no premature Step 3/4 coupling. |

## Overall: REWORK

## What I tried to falsify

- Read all four new files in full myself rather than trusting the Tester's excerpts.
- Grepped `zimmTokens.ts` directly for `background`/`bg-0` and confirmed the real registered names are `--zimm-color-bg-01` through `-07` — never `-background-NN`.
- Ran a repo-wide grep for `zimm-color-background` to rule out an alias I might not know about — zero hits outside this step's own two files.
- Cross-checked **every other** `var(--zimm-*)` reference in the same recipe (`--zimm-border-width-default`, `--zimm-color-border-focus`, `--zimm-focus-ring`, `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default`, `--zimm-scale-1200`) individually against the registry, specifically to test whether Finding A was symptomatic of a broader pattern of fabricated names — all five are real and correctly resolve. The defect is isolated to exactly one property, not systemic.
- Confirmed `colors.background['02']` literally equals `ivory[200]` in `colour.ts` — the fix is a pure rename to what the recipe's own comment already says it should be, not a fresh design decision.
- Ran `npx tsc --noEmit` myself (clean) and the actual `vitest` suite myself (152/152 green) rather than accepting "gates are green" as reported — I wanted to see the vacuous pass and the jsdom stderr noise with my own eyes.
- Read `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`/`booleanKeys`/`PROP_COMBINATIONS` generation logic line-by-line to verify Finding B's mechanism from source, not from the Tester's narrative — confirmed `selected` is absent from `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`, so it can never appear in any of the 32 generated combinations, so the `selected: true` branch is structurally unreachable by this guard.
- Located `recipeParts.test.ts` at its actual path (the Tester's report implied `theme/components/`; it's really `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`) and read enough of it to confirm it's a generic, non-hardcoded sibling walk that does cover this new component without needing a named case.
- Re-ran `git status`/`git diff --stat` myself to independently confirm the exact 2-line diff and the untouched hard-stop paths, rather than trusting the Orchestrator's restated numbers.

A verification pass that only reproduces what it's told to find isn't a real one — the five-token cross-check and the recipeGuards source read were both attempts to find a *different* or *broader* defect than the one already reported, and both came back clean, which is itself useful information (the defect is contained, not a symptom of a pattern).

## What I could not verify

- **The live-browser transparent-render itself, first-hand.** I did not spin up my own Playwright/Chromium run to watch the computed style. I'm relying on the Tester's real-browser run plus my own independent confirmation of the necessary precondition (the variable name is registered nowhere) plus deterministic, unambiguous CSS spec behaviour for an unresolvable `var()` with no fallback on a non-inherited property.
